html:
The global order is significantly reshaped today by a dramatic escalation in the US-Iran conflict, marked by a third consecutive night of US strikes on Iranian targets and President Trump's announcement of a new naval blockade and 20% charge on the Strait of Hormuz. These actions have drawn Iranian retaliation against tankers in the strait and Gulf nations, casting a long shadow over regional stability and global energy markets.

Middle East Tensions: The US launched its third night of strikes on Iran, coinciding with Trump's declaration of a 20% charge as part of a new blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. The UAE condemned Iran's 'brazen' attack on tankers, reporting one sailor killed, while Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility for striking two vessels and targeting Bahrain's Juffair base. Bahrain experienced air raid sirens and accused Iran of targeting civilians, and a vessel was hit by an unknown projectile near Oman. This heightened conflict has led to a 9% jump in oil prices and prompted US missions in the UAE to suspend consular appointments due to the 'security situation.' Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi maintained Iran's role as the "eternal guardian" of Hormuz and stated that US actions jeopardize regional peace.

US Foreign Policy: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a campaign to dismantle the international criminal court (ICC), claiming it interferes with US military and law enforcement operations. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom announced its intention to designate Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist group, linking it to antisemitic attacks. Amid the escalating conflict, Trump notified Congress of renewed military operations against Iran but also indicated that a deal with Tehran was still 'possible,' with an upcoming "speech to the nation" planned for Thursday.

European Security: Ukraine and key Western allies formed an air-defence coalition to jointly develop a new anti-ballistic missile system, even as Kyiv faced attacks. Russia's Ministry of Defense announced it targeted two cargo ships used by Ukrainian armed forces in the Odesa region, further deepening a Russian fuel crisis that has seen Ukraine strikes halt shipping on a key wheat route. Japan, meanwhile, acknowledged a growing need to counter espionage after a New York Times report identified the country as a "den of spies" and a hub for Russia to procure dual-use technology for its war in Ukraine.

US Domestic Issues: The US government has refunded $81 billion in Trump tariffs after the supreme court ruled them illegal, highlighting an ongoing impact of Donald Trump’s economic plan. Separately, an ICE agent fatally shot a Colombian national in Maine, the second such incident in less than a week, drawing scrutiny to immigration enforcement. In other news, Trump approved a sharp reduction in the size of two national monuments in Utah, opening nearly three million acres of sacred Native American land to corporate developers and the oil and gas industry.

Other Global Developments: Hungary's parliament voted to remove Tamás Sulyok from office, who was widely seen as a loyalist of former prime minister Viktor Orbán, who lost power in April. Europe also grappled with environmental and public safety concerns, as a wildfire south of Paris, which an interior minister suggested could have been set deliberately, raged, and thousands reportedly died in England and Wales from recent heat waves. Tributes poured in for 'Jurassic Park' actor Sam Neill, who died aged 78.
